investigations.title: Left-Wing Terrorism Is on the Rise
investigations.summary: Left-Wing Terrorism & Political Violence in the United States
investigations.story:
Left-wing terror attacks reach record highs in 2025 — fueled by unhinged opposition to Trump admin, disturbing study finds
eft-wing terror attacks are on track to reach a record high this year — as Democrats have been accused of ramping up their harmful rhetoric in their opposition to the Trump administration, a disturbing new study has found.

Violent plots planned or perpetrated by the far left in the US, as a percentage of all terrorist attacks and plots, hit a high in the first half of 2025, and are on pace to reach a three-decade high by the end of the year, according to a study from the Center for Strategic & International Studies.

Through July 4, 2025 — thus excluding the assassination of Charlie Kirk and the attack on the Dallas ICE facility — there were five left-wing attacks or plots, the study found.

Researchers noted that the increase in left-wing violence since President Trump first took office in 2016 has been largely motivated by anti-government extremism or partisan extremism.

Since then, “all left-wing attacks through July 4, 2025, appeared to be motivated by one of these ideologies,” the study found, noting that Kirk’s fatal shooting appears to fit the pattern.

Kirk’s alleged killer, 22-year-old Tyler Robinson, scrawled “Hey fascist, catch this” on a shell casing before shooting him dead on Sept. 10, law enforcement officials said.
findings: Finding #1. CSIS says 2025 was the first time in 30+ years that left-wing terrorist attacks outnumbered far-right attacks, while also noting right-wing terrorism remains historically larger over recent decades.

Finding #2. Left-wing actors responsible for more attacks this year, report says” — Washington Post discussing CSIS findings that left-wing attacks surpassed right-wing attacks during parts of 2025 for the first time in decades.

Left-Wing Terrorism and Political Violence in the United States: What the Data Tells Us” — CSIS analysis explaining that attacks tied to anti-government, anti-ICE, anti-corporate, and extremist activist motives increased sharply.

timeline.event: Donald Trump begins second presidential term. Nationwide anti-Trump demonstrations intensify, anti-ICE activism surges, extremist rhetoric online increases according to CSIS reports.

Escalation in Anti-ICE and Anti-Government Violence. Federal agencies report increase in attacks on ICE facilities, vandalism, arson attempts, clashes at demonstrations, and anti-police rhetoric tied to extremist activist circles. CSIS later stated left-wing attacks in 2025 outnumbered right-wing attacks for the first time in decades.

Tesla Dealership / Anti-Musk Attacks. Multiple incidents involving arson, vandalism, Molotov cocktails, and anti-Elon Musk slogans targeted Tesla-related property. AG Pam Bondi publicly referred to several incidents as 'domestic terrorism.'

"86 47" Controversy. Former FBI Director James Comey posted an image reading "86 47." Trump allies interpreted it as a coded threat against the 47th president. Comey denied violent intent, but it fueled national debate over escalating political rhetoric.

Multiple Threats Against Donald Trump. Federal authorities investigated threats and plots involving online assassination rhetoric, extremist anti-Trump postings, and threats against campaign events and federal facilities. DOJ and Secret Service expanded threat monitoring.

North Texas ICE Detention Center Attack. A protest escalated into violence — a police officer was shot, multiple suspects charged, and prosecutors alleged links to extremist anti-fascist ideology. The DOJ described the group as a North Texas 'antifa cell.'

Charlie Kirk Assassination. Conservative activist Charlie Kirk was killed in a high-profile shooting. Federal investigators examined ideological motive, online extremism, anti-conservative rhetoric, and possible political targeting. The case dramatically intensified national debate over left-wing political violence.

Continued Anti-ICE Violence and Threats. Federal officials repeatedly warned of organized anti-ICE hostility, violent rhetoric online, and escalating confrontations surrounding immigration enforcement. The administration classified some extremist anti-fascist networks as terrorist-related threats.

investigations.title: Dark Money & Digital Influence
investigations.summary: Paid To Persuade? The Dark Money Behind Political Influencers
investigations.story:
August 27, 2025, 6:00 AM. The Wire Published a story by Taylor Lorenz titled; A Dark Money Group Is Secretly Funding High-Profile Democratic Influencers. An initiative aimed at boosting Democrats online offers influencers up to $8,000 a month to push the party line. All they have to do is keep it secret and agree to restrictions on their content. 

November 2025, Chairman James Comer announced a formal investigation after reports alleged that the Chorus program paid influencers to amplify Democratic political messaging while restricting disclosure of those financial relationships.

The House Oversight investigation has evolved from a media-report inquiry into a broader probe examining whether the Chorus Creator Incubator Program and related organizations attempted to avoid campaign-finance disclosure rules and obscure operational control structures.

Key Entities Involved
House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform
James Comer
Sixteen Thirty Fund
Arabella Advisors
Sunflower Services
Creator Collective
Chorus Creator Incubator Program

By spring 2026, Comer stated the Committee believed compliance had been incomplete, leading to escalated pressure and additional document demands.

On May 14, 2026, House Oversight Committee Chairman James Comer issued a subpoena to the Sixteen Thirty Fund demanding documents and communications tied to the Chorus Creator Incubator Program.

The subpoena was sent to:

Amy Kurtz, President of Sixteen Thirty Fund.

According to the House Oversight Committee, the investigation is examining whether the Chorus influencer network:

attempted to avoid federal campaign-finance disclosure requirements,
coordinated political messaging through paid influencers,
and operated as what Comer called a “dark money operation.”

The Committee stated that:

“influencers paid through the Chorus program generated content advocating for candidates, ballot initiatives, and political parties in U.S. elections.”
Comer also claimed Sixteen Thirty Fund’s response to earlier document requests was inadequate, saying the organization had only produced:

135 pages since November 2025.

Another major issue raised in the subpoena:

The Committee alleged the program’s legal structure changed shortly after congressional scrutiny began, potentially to obscure records or operational control.

The Oversight Committee specifically referenced concerns involving:

contracts,
internal communications,
funding documents,
creator agreements,
organizational charts,
and communications involving influencers and political figures.



The “Restructuring” Issue

One of the biggest developments came in March 2026.

Comer alleged that after the Committee requested records:

Sixteen Thirty Fund distanced itself from Chorus,
a new entity called Creator Collective appeared,
and operational control allegedly shifted shortly after congressional scrutiny began.

The Committee described the sequence as:

“dubious at best”

and suggested it may have been designed to:

shield records,
obscure ownership/control,
or complicate congressional oversight.

Committee’s Main Concern

The investigation is centered on whether the structure functioned as:

coordinated political influence disguised as independent creator content.

The Committee argues that if influencers were compensated to push political narratives while withholding disclosure, that could raise:

campaign-finance issues,
ethics concerns,
transparency problems,
and potential FEC reporting questions

The Sixteen Thirty Fund responded publicly saying it:

“complies with the law and has cooperated with the Committee’s inquiry while protecting the rights and safety of the people who work with us.”

Defenses From Chorus-Linked Figures

People connected to the program disputed many allegations.

Some creators argued:

Chorus was more of a creator-support or networking initiative,
not a covert political operation,
and that reporting exaggerated the contracts.

Brian Tyler Cohen reportedly compared the initiative to a “scholarship program” rather than an illegal influence operation.

Elizabeth Booker Houston publicly argued:

Chorus did not control her independent interviews,
Sixteen Thirty Fund was merely a fiscal sponsor,
and some media reporting was inaccurate.

Why This Investigation Matters

This probe is significant because it sits at the intersection of:

influencer marketing,
political campaigning,
nonprofit “dark money” networks,
and digital media disclosure laws.

Congress is effectively asking:

When does a paid influencer stop being an “independent creator” and become part of a coordinated political communications operation?

That question has implications far beyond this case and could affect:

future influencer disclosure rules,
political podcast sponsorships,
TikTok creator funding,
nonprofit media operations,
and online campaign coordination.


The Sixteen Thirty Fund’s Larger Role

The Sixteen Thirty Fund has long been described by critics and media outlets as one of the largest Democratic-aligned “dark money” hubs in American politics. It operates through nonprofit/fiscal sponsorship structures tied historically to Arabella Advisors.

The organization has spent hundreds of millions on:

ballot initiatives,
advocacy campaigns,
voter mobilization,
issue advertising,
and progressive infrastructure.

The Chorus investigation is the first major congressional attempt to examine whether those same nonprofit-network strategies were adapted to the influencer economy
findings: Finding #1. WIRED reported that the Chorus Creator Incubator Program, backed through the Sixteen Thirty Fund, offered Democratic-leaning influencers up to $8,000/month under contracts with secrecy/disclosure restrictions.
Finding #2.The House Oversight Committee opened an investigation in November 2025, saying the program reportedly paid participants to promote Democratic messaging under secrecy contracts.
Finding #3.  On May 14, 2026, the Committee said it subpoenaed Sixteen Thirty Fund documents after limited compliance.
